figures.caption: Figure 3. (a) Compilation of isostatic pressing parameters used in the SSB literature for densification and integration of solid electrolytes and cells, respectively. Largely CIP is the primary technique that is leveraged within the SSB community. Shaded markers indicate either HIP or WIP cycles. The color of the markers indicates the solid electrolyte material family (pink markers, LLZO; yellow markers, Na-based NASICONs; green markers, sulfides; gray marker, hybrid electrolyte). The data for this figure are collected from refs 33, 34, 36−56. (b) XRD patterns and optical images of LLZO before and after the HIP treatment. The scale bars represent 10 mm. Data adapted from ref 33. SEM images of anti-perovskite solid electrolytes processed under (c) uniaxial loading conditions, (d) CIP conditions, and (e) WIP conditions. The scale bars in all the SEM images are 10 μm. (f, g) Tomographic reconstruction slices and pore volume visualization of the anti-perovskites processed under CIP and WIP conditions along with the measured porosity. The sub-volume investigated for porosity evaluation and visualized here is 300 × 300 × 300 μm3.

note_manual: Printed inconsistencies visible in the crops (details in the digest §3-8 / §11): (1) the article text cites 'Figure S2' for WIP in standard CIP vessels and 'Figure S1' for the vessel size (3 m × 5 m, placed after the HIP description) while the SI captions read S1 = CIP/WIP equipment, S2 = HIP equipment; (2) text 'Standard HIP … up to 200 MPa (30 000 psi)' vs Table 1 '207/30'; (3) text 'one WIP cycle every 10−20 min' and 'one operation cycle per minute or faster' vs Fig. 5b cycles/hour 1.2 (WIP) and 2 (CIP); (4) the anti-perovskite is written 'Li3OHCl' (SI S1) and 'LiOHCl' (SI S2, Fig. S5 caption); (5) Fig. 3 caption (c) 'uniaxial loading conditions' vs panel title 'Green Pellet'; the 12 % porosity of that pellet is given in the text only (no tomogram shown) and its pressing pressure is not stated anywhere; (6) Fig. 3f/3g slice scale bars are printed '10 μm' (bar = 110 px of a 379–382 px wide slice → the slice would be ≈35 μm wide if the label is right) while the evaluated sub-volume is 300 × 300 × 300 μm3 — the paper does not say whether the slice is a zoomed detail, so this is flagged as 'does not seem to match', not as a certain error; (7) LLTO Young's modulus printed '∼223 MPa' vs '192 MPa' (ref 64); (8) text 'pellet densities ranging from 85 to 100%' vs one 84 % entry in the SI spreadsheet and in Fig. S3; (9) Fig. 3a marker colours are not fully explained by the four-entry caption legend (pink LLZO, yellow Na-based NASICONs, green sulfides, gray hybrid): two green shades (bright green; dark teal) and an orange occur — matched against the spreadsheet, dark teal = sulfide cells (edge of the ≈490 MPa WIP marker, ≈400, ≈80 MPa) and bright green = Li-NASICON (solid-electrolyte column ≈200 MPa; cell column ≈500 MPa = the LATP full cell at 504 MPa; Fig. S3 / Fig. 4a also use green for Li-NASICON), while the two solid-electrolyte markers at ≈506 MPa (LATP rows in the spreadsheet) are pink; there is no sulfide marker in the solid-electrolyte column, and a pink cell marker at ≈20 MPa has no matching row; (10) Fig. 5e / spreadsheet: the 'Cell Integration – CIP' column divides by 10^7 where all other cost columns divide by 10^6; (11) spreadsheet: electrode area computed from pack-level capacity Wh / 900 V.
